On macOS and Linux, an inherited pipe makes the server stop its dedicated process group when the owner host dies, including after a hard kill.
If the child is still present, its ownership record is missing, or the socket has an active listener, recovery refuses and requires inspection.
Each accepted `ops run` creates a local operation record with recipe/profile revisions, typed intent, start/end events and a compact outcome.
The store retains at most 500 records per profile by pruning the oldest completed records, and refuses new work if unfinished records alone fill the cap.
An unfinished record after a caller crash is labelled `completion_unverified`; it does not prove the operation is still running or safely stopped.
The journal does not store credentials, prompts, full calibration reports or raw server traces.
Its files use mode 0600 and directories mode 0700 on POSIX; Windows ACL behavior still needs release qualification.

When `--max-queue` is set, at most **effective slots + max queue** HTTP inference calls are reserved at once.

The cap applies to OpenAI chat completions, Anthropic messages and OpenAI Responses, including streaming calls; excess calls get HTTP 429 with code `admission_full` and `Retry-After: 1` before any SSE headers.
The reservation includes model loading, prompt preparation and any server-side MCP rounds, so it is a conservative pressure bound, not an exact count of engine-queued requests.
`--queue-timeout` requires the cap and limits the wait for the first engine turn after prompt preparation.
A timed-out nonstreaming call gets HTTP 429 with code `queue_wait_timeout` and `Retry-After: 1`; a streaming call gets a format-specific error event because its SSE headers are already sent.
